subject: Day 50: have infant Tylenol ready
bodyText:
Today's focus
Avi is 50 days old, mid-week 8, and the 2-month vaccine round is days away. This week is about staging the post-vaccine response so a predictable 24-48h of fussiness does not turn into a scramble.

Action items
- Stock infant acetaminophen now and confirm the weight-based dose with your pediatrician before the visit. Treat after the shots if needed, not before; prophylactic dosing can blunt the antibody response. AAP on immunizations: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/immunizations/aap-policy-on-immunizations/
- Print your 2-month question list (sleep training, solids timing at 4 vs 6 months, growth percentile trajectory, when to drop the swaddle); a 20-30 minute visit goes fast. AAP periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/care-delivery-approaches/periodicity-schedule/
- Block the 48 hours after the visit lightly so one parent can be home for expected drowsiness and feeding disruption.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Witching-hour fussiness in the early evening and a stronger startle to loud sounds; both are typical at this age and resolve without intervention.
- [monitor] No social smile yet by week 8. Note it and raise it at the 2-month visit rather than waiting; about 90% of infants smile responsively by now.
- [call within 24h] Persistent vomiting beyond 24 hours, or refusal of multiple feeds in a row with a drop in wet diapers.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C) in an infant under 90 days, blue lips, labored breathing, or a seizure-like episode warrants a same-day call or 911!

Enrichment opportunities
- Pair one specific song with every diaper change so Avi learns to predict the sequence; live, participatory singing is the active ingredient, not recording quality. Gerry et al. on infant music: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/
- Keep the daily read-aloud at roughly a 3:1 repeat-to-novel ratio so familiar rhythm and predictability do the cognitive work. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/
- Stagger tummy time into four to six short bouts toward 45-60 minutes cumulative; short sessions after feeds beat one long protest. HealthyChildren tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit; vaccines HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, IPV #1.
- Day 57-72: post-vaccine 24-48h window of fussiness, low-grade fever, and extra drowsiness.
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit; vaccines RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete

- Holds head up while on tummy
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained head lift of several seconds, not just a brief bob. Forearms may or may not be supporting yet.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-head-up-tummy/complete

- Hands relax open most of the time
  AAP window: day 35-90
  What to look for: Newborn fists relax as the palmar grasp reflex fades. Predictor of voluntary grasp coming.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hands-open-mostly/complete

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete
